Maya Chen: Quick share — ran an apples-to-apples run comparing synthetic floodbench vs. replay harness for cross-region failover. Dropping notes + artifacts.
Maya Chen: artifacts: <https://artifacts.internal/redwood/perf/2012345678>
Ryan Patel: Nice. what's the main delta?
Maya Chen: Key diffs: replay shows KV-cache warmup path reduces p50 by ~12% but exposes p99 tail when kernel selection flips during fallback; synthetic hides the tail because arrival shapes are smoother.
Anita Gomez: Can you paste the harness command?
Maya Chen: ```
./replay_harness --trace=prod-2026-02 --regions=us-west,eu-west --failover=auto --fallback-model=rwkv-quant-v2
``` 
Leo Park: Did you control for batch_size heuristics? Those can change kernel picks.
Maya Chen: Yes — we forced batching policy 'latency-prefer' vs 'throughput-prefer' and logged kernel picks per request. Results attached: <https://artifacts.internal/redwood/perf/2012345678/kernel-picks.csv>
perf-bot: benchmark artifact uploaded — summary: us-west p50 68ms p95 190ms p99 420ms; eu-west p50 82ms p95 240ms p99 690ms (quant fallback case).
Ryan Patel: Surprising that quant fallback increased p99 by ~270ms in eu-west during drain. Any idea?
Anita Gomez: Maybe kernel switch + KV miss compounding. Did you capture KV cache hit histograms?
Maya Chen: Yes — replay shows a spike of cold misses right after drain window; KV priming needs ~15s at our request rate. Recommend priming via synthetic prefix replays in region before traffic shift. :thumbsup:
Leo Park: Agree. Also consider sticky routing for 10s to let KV prime. That trades a small latency bump for far fewer p99 spikes.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback trigger set for routing policy change. Ping @infra if we roll.
Ryan Patel: I'll run follow-up: sticky=10s + batch-policy=adaptive + quant-fallback run. ETA EOD.
Maya Chen: Thanks — raw logs + kernel-pick CSVs uploaded. Opening PR for test config by EOD.
